extracted.intended_audience: persons wishing to register trade marks (applicants, agents, proprietors, Cutlers' Company members)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and procedural rules under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act 1883 for preparing, filing, advertising, opposing, and maintaining trade mark registrations in the UK (including special provisions for Sheffield/Cutlers' marks and cotton classes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to register pending determination of conflicting claims (special case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comptroller refuses to register any mark where there are conflicting claims until their rights have been determined according to law; the manner in which the rights of such claimants may be submitted to the Court by the Comptroller or, if the Comptroller so require, by the claimants, shall, unless the Court otherwise order, be by a special case; and such special case shall be filed and proceeded with in like manner as any other special case submitted to the Court, or in such other manner as the Court may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement of special cases: where the special case is to be submitted to the parties it may be agreed to by them, or if they differ, may be settled by the Comptroller on payment of the prescribed fees. The fees for settling the special case is 21. See First Schedule. Form of Request: Form 80.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification/alteration entry after Court order
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an order has been made by the Court (e.g., allowing an appeal under section 62, disallowing an opposition under section 69, or under sections 72, 90, or 92), the person in whose favour such order has been made shall forthwith leave at the Patent Office an office copy of such order; the register shall thereupon be rectified or altered, or the purport of such order shall otherwise be duly entered in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant (or one directed by Comptroller) must supply office copy to trigger rectification/entry in register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal from register and recording cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a trade mark has been removed from the register for nonpayment of the prescribed fee or otherwise under the provisions of section 79, the Comptroller shall cause to be entered in the register a record of such removal and the cause thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms of Application and declaration to cancel a mark: Forms O and P. See also S. 91.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration of proprietor's address
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registered proprietor of a trade mark sends to the Comptroller, together with the prescribed fee, a notice of an alteration in his address, the Comptroller shall alter the register accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of Notice: Form M. Fee payable: 5s. See First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of rectification or variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an order is made by the Court for making, expunging, or varying an entry in the register, the Comptroller shall, if he thinks that such variation or rectification should be made public, and at the expense of the person applying for the same, publish, by advertisement or otherwise, in such manner as he thinks just, the circumstances attending the rectification or variation in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of Alteration: Form N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to Comptroller before applying to Court to add/alter mark (s.92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the registered proprietor intends to apply for the leave of the Court to add to or to alter such trade mark under section 92, the notice to be given to the Comptroller shall be given fourteen days at least before such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If leave be granted, applicant must forthwith supply to the Comptroller such a number of representations of the trade mark as altered as he may deem sufficient. Fee payable on rectification of the Register is 10s. See First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hours of public inspection of the Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register of Trade Marks shall be open to the public, on payment of the prescribed fee, on every weekday between the hours of ten and four, except on specified holidays and times (Christmas Day, Good Friday, Queen's birthday observance, Bank of England holidays, days notified by placard at Patent Office, or times when register required for official use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee for searching register or classified representations of Trade Marks is 1s for every quarter of an hour. See First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to dispense with required acts/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person is required to do any act, sign any document, make any declaration, or produce any document or evidence to or left with the Comptroller and it is shown to the satisfaction of the Comptroller that from any reasonable cause such person is unable to do so, it shall be lawful for the Comptroller, with the sanction of the Board of Trade, and upon production of such other evidence, and subject to such terms as they may think fit, to dispense with any such act, document, declaration, or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also S. 99.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of trade mark documents and correction of irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document or drawing or other representation of a trade mark for the amending of which no special provision is made by the Act may be amended, and any irregularity in procedure which, in the opinion of the Comptroller, may be obviated without detriment to the interests of any person may be corrected, if the Comptroller think fit, and on such terms as he may direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement of prescribed time by Comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: The time prescribed by these Rules for doing any act, or taking any proceeding thereunder, may be enlarged by the Comptroller, if he think fit; and upon such notice to other parties, and proceedings thereon, and upon such terms, as he may direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications to Cutlers' Company (Sheffield marks) — form and duplicates
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications to the Cutlers' Company for registration of a trade mark under section 81 shall be in duplicate, accompanied by the prescribed fees and representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are the same as for other marks. See First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutlers' Company must notify Comptroller and supply representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cutlers' Company shall, within seven days of the receipt by them of an application to register a trade mark, send the Comptroller one copy of such application, by way of notice thereof, together with two representations of the mark for each class for which the applicant seeks registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's time to object to Cutlers' Company application
rubrics_metrics.description: The time within which the Comptroller shall give notice to the Cutlers' Company of any objection he may have to the acceptance of an application made to the Company shall be one month from the date of receipt by the Comptroller of the notice made at Sheffield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no such objection is made, the Cutlers' Company shall require the applicant to send a wood block or electrotype as the Comptroller may direct, and the Comptroller shall, if satisfied with such wood block or electrotype, advertise the application in the same manner as an application made to him at the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of general Rules to Cutlers' Company proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of these Rules as to forms, representations, the proceedings on opposition to registration, and all subsequent proceedings shall, as far as the circumstances allow, apply to all applications to register made to the Cutlers' Company, and to all proceedings consequent thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of Appeal from Cutlers' Company at Sheffield: Form W.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's certificates and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller, when required for any legal proceeding or other special purpose to give a certificate as to any entry, matter, or thing which he is authorised by the Act or Rules to make or do, may, on receipt of a request in writing, and on payment of the prescribed fee, give such certificate, and shall specify on the face of it the legal proceeding or other purpose for which such certificate is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms: general certificate Form U; for use in legal proceedings Form S. Fee for certificate for use in legal proceedings is 10s. See First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and persons before whom statutory declarations must be made
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory declarations required by the Act and Rules, or used in proceedings thereunder, must, if made in the United Kingdom, be made before any justice of the peace, or any commissioner or other officer authorised by law in any part of the United Kingdom to administer an oath for the purpose of any legal proceeding; if made in any other part of Her Majesty's dominions, before any court, judge, justice of the peace, or officer authorised by law to administer an oath there for legal proceedings; if made out of Her Majesty's dominions, before a British Minister, Consul, Vice-consul, notary public, or before a judge or magistrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission without proof of the genuineness of seals/signatures on declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document purporting to have affixed, impressed, or subscribed thereto the seal or signature of any person authorised to take such declaration, in testimony of such declaration having been made and subscribed before him, may be admitted by the Comptroller without proof of the genuineness of such seal or signature, or of the official character of such person or his authority to take such declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to address communications and language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications relating to Trade Marks, not being Sheffield marks, should be addressed to the Comptroller, Patent Office, Trade Marks Branch. All applications should be in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may be made by post, or left at the Patent Office, Trade Marks Branch, 25 Southampton Buildings, Chancery Lane, London, W.C. Agents with multiple applications should make separate letters per application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees via stamped forms (places and method)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees in relation to Trade Marks Registration cannot be received at the Patent Office. They should be paid in exchange for the stamped forms required, which may be obtained at designated Inland Revenue and Post Office locations and Chief Post Offices (list provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of places where stamped forms may be obtained is enumerated in para. 2; stamped forms correspond to specific Form letters and fees listed in para. 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Trade Mark (essential particulars)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of the Act, a Trade Mark must consist of or contain at least one of the following essential particulars: (1) A name of an individual or firm printed, impressed, or woven in some particular and distinctive manner; or (2) A written signature or copy of a written signature of the individual or firm applying; or (3) A distinctive device, mark, brand, heading, label, ticket, or fancy word or words not in common use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be added to any of these particulars any letters, words or figures, or combination thereof. Any special and distinctive word(s), letter, or figure used as a Trade Mark before 13 August 1875 may be registered under this part of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to search before adopting a Trade Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: A person wishing to adopt a Trade Mark should, before engraving a block and circulating impressions among customers, make a search or a formal application at the Trade Marks Branch to ascertain whether the proposed mark is already registered or would be refused under section 72 as calculated to deceive by resemblance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee for making a search amongst classified representations of Trade Marks is 1s for each quarter of an hour. Fee for a formal Application is 5s. The Comptroller does not undertake to make searches except in connection with formal applications for registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constituents of an application for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An application consists of: (a) an Application Form (Form 'F') giving certain particulars and bearing an impressed stamp of 5s; and (b) certain additional representations of the Trade Mark mounted on forms (Form 'G').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should read marginal notes before filling form. A separate Application Form is required for each class. Representation of the mark should be placed in the centre of the Application Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing requirements for firms, companies and agents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the mark is property of a firm, application should be signed by a member of the firm who should add 'A Member of the Firm' after signature; if of a Company, by the Secretary or principal officer who should add 'For the Company'; applications may be made by Agents in the name of and on behalf of owners, but the Agent must be duly authorised and the necessary authority signed by the owner(s). Applications made by Agents should have 'Agent' after the agent's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special particulars for certain goods and non-Roman characters
rubrics_metrics.description: When a mark is used on metal goods other than cutlery/edge tools/raw steel, the Application Form should state of what metal(s) the goods are made. When the mark includes words printed in other than Roman characters, a translation of such words, signed by the Applicant or Agent, should be given at the back or foot of the Application Form and each additional representation. For marks claimed in Classes 23–25, the Applicant should state by what name the particular mark would be referred to in the invoices of his house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 12, Rule 15 and class-specific notes (e.g., cotton goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional representations requirements (number, form, and execution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each additional representation should be placed in the centre of a separate form (Form 'G'). For a Trade Mark not claimed in Classes 23–35, two Additional Representations are required for each class claimed. For a Trade Mark claimed in any one or more of Classes 23–35, three Additional Representations should be sent for each such class. The representations on the Form 'G' must agree in every respect with each other and with that on Form 'F'. Representations of large size may be folded but must be backed with linen and firmly affixed; representations must not be executed in pencil; they should be durable and suitable for preservation and binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of a series of Trade Marks (Section 66)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comptroller is empowered to register under one registration a series of Trade Marks which, while resembling each other in material particulars, differ in statements of the goods for which they are used, statements of numbers, statements of price, statements of quality, or statements of names of places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application is made for such a series, a representation of each of the marks included in the series must be affixed to Form 'F' and to each of the Forms 'G'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common or Open Marks and disclaimer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a Trade Mark used before 13 August 1875, Common or Open Marks of any kind may be registered in connection with it; but if the Trade Mark is not so used, Common or Open Marks consisting of a word or combination of words only can be registered as a part of the Mark. In each case the Applicant for entry of such common particular(s) must disclaim the right to the exclusive use of the same in a note at the back or foot of the Application Form and each additional representation, such note to be signed by the Applicant or Agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 74 (definition of Common Marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on classification of goods
rubrics_metrics.description: A Guide to the Classification of Goods under the Trade Marks Rules, 1883, can be obtained on application at the Patent Office, Trade Marks Branch, and should be asked for if the Applicant feels difficulty determining to which class(es) the goods belong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third Schedule to the Rules contains the Classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement prerequisite before entry on Register
rubrics_metrics.description: A Trade Mark cannot in any case be entered upon the Register until two months after its advertisement in the Official Paper (Trade Marks Journal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wood-blocks/electrotypes for advertisement — supply and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A Wood-block or Electrotype must be furnished for each Mark in each Class claimed (except Classes 23, 24, and 25 for which no Blocks or Electrotypes are required), but no Block or Electrotype should be forwarded until a formal demand is sent by the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blocks/electrotypes must correspond exactly with the Representations, afford perfectly distinct impressions, be on a scale sufficiently large to reproduce the Marks faithfully; worn or mutilated Blocks cannot be accepted. Largest space available is 8.5 x 10 inches. When depth exceeds 2 inches, charge 2s for every inch or part thereof beyond 2 inches. The Number given by the Comptroller should not be cut on the face but marked on the side. Send with Form 2 and guidance representation. Blocks/electrotypes supplied for advertisement cannot be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on claiming ornamental or coloured groundworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Ornamental or coloured groundwork, such as tartans or checks, cannot be claimed as part of a Mark unless such groundwork be included within the Mark by some border or lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 67.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of certain emblems and words in marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Arms, or arms so nearly resembling them as to be calculated to deceive, and the words 'Registered', 'Registered Design', 'Copyright', 'Entered at Stationers' Hall', 'To counterfeit this is forgery', 'Patent', 'Patented' will not be registered under the Act, and should not appear upon the Representations of Trade Marks forming part of an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of representations of royalty, national emblems and medals (unless pre-1875 use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations of Her Majesty the Queen, or of any member of the Royal family; representations of the Royal Crown; national arms or flags; prize or exhibition medals will not be registered as Trade Marks, or as prominent parts of Trade Marks, unless the Marks have been used before 13 August 1875.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim must correspond to goods indicated on the face of a mark
rubrics_metrics.description: When there appears on the face of a Trade Mark an indication of the goods to which the Mark is applied, the claim for its registration must be in respect of those goods only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for counter-statement and bond in opposition proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescribed form of Counter-statement and a Form of Bond (security for costs) are provided for opposition proceedings under the Act; the bond binds parties to pay such costs as the High Court of Justice may think fit to award in respect of the opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before being required to bring an opposition matter before the Court under Rule 29, the Applicant is afforded opportunity of objecting, if he thinks fit, to the solvency of the security for costs which may be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must accompany application in impressed stamps
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application for the Registration of a Trade Mark will not be entered by the Comptroller unless it be accompanied by the proper fees in impressed stamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the First Schedule to the Trade Mark Rules, 1883, and the List of Forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutlers' Company application procedure and addressing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications made to the Cutlers' Company pursuant to section 81 should be made on Form 'C' (address in left-hand corner 'To the Cutlers Company, Sheffield') and should be left at or sent by post to the Cutlers Hall, Sheffield. Each application should be accompanied by an unstamped copy on foolscap paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postal address for Cutlers' Company: Chas. Macro Wilson, Esq., The Law Clerk, The Cutlers Hall, Sheffield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manchester office for cotton classes — local searches
rubrics_metrics.description: An office will be opened at 48 Royal Exchange, Manchester, where searches can be made on payment of 1s for each quarter of an hour for all Marks in classes of Textiles from Class 23 to Class 35.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience for merchants and manufacturers engaged in the Cotton Trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Comptroller's certificates and how to request them
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller's Certificate in relation to a Trade Mark is of four kinds: (i) for use in legal proceedings; (ii) for use in applying for registration in foreign countries; (iii) of any application made and proceedings thereon; (iv) a certificate of refusal of a Mark in use before 13 August 1875 and not registerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a certificate forward the appropriate Form (Form T, S, U, or Z as applicable) with the Comptroller's official number of the Mark and state the purpose (legal proceedings, foreign registration, or other).
